title: I have completed my very first game in 3D. This isn't a high profile or anything like that but it works
author: Chelsea_Grimes
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/i8ueuu741txh1.png

I have always wanted to make a 3D game but never tried because I assumed that I would need a bunch of people to complete the game. I thought that I would need a programmer and another person for modeling and the last person for thorough finishing of the project. It was not a technical limitation really - it was knowing how to divide the work into sections that I could actually finish by myself.

I made everything based on Tripo Vibe Gaming playbook, which is an open source manual published by Tripo for making games. It is not a programming platform and does not write any codes for you. Instead, it divides the process of making a game into six different phases which helps.

https://i.redd.it/2c6xwin51txh1.png

Most of my time has been spent on two opposite ends of the spectrum. Firstly, I took ages trying to figure out the loop of Pit Nine. Secondly, by the time I was done with everything, I took the whole bunch of models and placed them in the scrapyard after making necessary changes in the alignment.

So this is what Pit Nine looks like now: it has a scrapyard, two sets of machine hounds, and the final battle with the Foreman. The length of the whole game is only a few minutes, but it is functional, and you can play it in a browser.

If you have any good suggestions for improvement, I would be very happy to hear them.
